name: Runner Extras - Query Join Aggregation OOS
brief: Follow-up to issue #2137: a query column with Method = Sum/Count/Average/Min/Max used to silently return unaggregated, ungrouped rows instead of aggregating or throwing. This suite originally pinned the two surfaces that still could not aggregate correctly as loud RunnerOutOfScopeException throws; issue #2146 has since implemented both for real (a multi-dataitem JOIN query with an aggregated column, and a runtime SetFilter/SetRange on an aggregated column — a HAVING-clause filter), so the tests below now assert the correct aggregated/filtered answer instead of an expected throw.
description: The general BC-language claim these fixes make — a query with Method = Sum/Count/Average/Min/Max implicitly groups by its other (non-aggregated) columns and computes the aggregate per group, exactly like the SQL SELECT ... GROUP BY / HAVING the real service tier compiles, whether the query is single-dataitem or a multi-dataitem JOIN — is plain BC behaviour, and IS NOW COVERED upstream in the al-language corpus: it merged as StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#74 (commit 6262dd6506dd20a39ee1626ed6a0ddd24d0685cd) and passes on both BC 27.5 and BC 28.3, and the submodule pin in this repo was bumped to it alongside the #2146 fix. Two of the four tests below (JoinWithAggregateColumn_GroupsJoinedRowsAndAggregates, SetFilterOnAggregateColumn_EvaluatesAgainstGroupResult) now duplicate that upstream coverage and are a TRIMMING CANDIDATE for a follow-up cleanup PR. The other two (JoinWithoutAggregateColumn_StillReturnsJoinedRows, SetFilterOnNonAggregateColumn_StillWorks) are negative siblings pinning a narrower, still-uncovered claim: that the GROUP BY/HAVING code paths this fix added are correctly SCOPED to queries that actually have an aggregated column, and do not misfire on an ordinary join or an ordinary WHERE-style filter just because the query also happens to have an aggregate column somewhere. This suite is NOT being trimmed in this PR to avoid unrelated count-baseline churn; see the codeunit header for the same accounting.
